This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 30.11.2021 at about 1.00 p.m. petitioner had been riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-41- EC-9167 on Nelamangala - Magadi Nice Road, near SCCH-5 Gangondanahalli Bridge, Bengaluru, at that time, a driver of the Lorry bearing temporary registration No. MH-12-TR-DXN-0740 has parked the lorry in the center of the road without following traffic rules, taking any precaution barricade and without putting parking light, due to that, petitioner hit his motor cycle against lorry back side.
Consequent to which, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Kenganar Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years, working as coolie, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he cannot do his regular activities, further he SCCH-5 has lost his income and future prospective life, happiness and earning capacity.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing temporary registration No.MH-12-TR-DXN-740 and Nelamangala Police have registered a case in crime No.440/2021 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the R.C.Owner and 2nd Respondent being the insurer of the offending lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the court and filed written statement and denied contents and allegations in the claim petition.

Further submitted that, new TATA vehicle model No.1412LPT Chassis SCCH-5 No.MAT86009M7K18182 was invoiced in his name and said vehicle was left from Pune on 27.11.021 through ZED YEM Logistics with TCR No.MH-TR-DXN-740 and said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 vide its No.CTP102476 dated 26.11.2021.
Further submitted that, alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the court through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further denied issuance of policy of insurance in respect of lorry bearing temporary registration No.MH-12-TR-DXN-740 and liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the Arun Kumar Vishwakarma vs V.S.T. Motors Pvt Ltd on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48251891/
2 SCCH-5 policy.

sentences.text: Further denied age, occupation, income, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and alleged involvement of insured vehicle etc., Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, on 30.11.2021 at about 1.00 p.m. when the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle at Nelamangala Magadi Nice Road, near Gangondanahalli Bridge, Bengaluru, at that time, one Lorry bearing Reg.
No.MH-12-TR-DXN- 740 was parking in the centre of the road, due to that,
petitioner hit to the lorry backside and fell down and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so from which respondent?
SCCH-5 3.
What order
or award?

7. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS as PW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, Senior Manager of respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and marked document as per Ex.R.1 and closed evidence 8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner inorder to prove his case, he himself examined as PW-1 and in his chief- examination evidence, he has reiterated petition averments.
Though he has been elaborately cross- examined by the Respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the petitioner.

10. Further to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon and SOADS, who examined the petitioner and has stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of SCCH-5 sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
12.
Per contra, Senior Manager in respondent No.1 company by name C.Haridass Miller is examined as RW-1 and marked authorization letter as Ex.R.1.
except oral evidence of RW-1, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 30.11.2021 at about 1.00 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-41-EC-9167 at Nelamangala - Magadi Nice Road, near Gangondanahalli Bridge, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the SCCH-5 petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
13. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the lorry bearing temporary Reg. No.MH-12-TR-DXN-740.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left proximal tibia fracture with avulsion of the fibula tip and impending compartment syndrome, for which he was treated with ORIF with proximal tibia LCP.

To prove the nature of the injuries sustained and treatment taken by him, he has SCCH-5 furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 30.11.2021 to 04.12.2021 i.e., for 5 days.

Further he has exhibited medical bills to the tune of Rs.1,45,051/- marked as Ex.P.10, medical prescription marked as Ex.P.11, advance receipts marked as Ex.P.12.
15.
In order to prove his case, he examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS as PW-2, who has exhibited clinical notes marked as Ex.P.15 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
In his affidavit evidence he has deposed that, petitioner suffers total physical disability of the left lower limb at 40% and whole body disability at 13%.
In cross-examination PW-2 has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the SCCH-5 petitioner and he has seen the discharge summary and wound certificate while assessing disability.
Further deposed that, fractures are united.
Further deposed that, loss of muscle power at the knee joint is due to non usage of the limb and disability assessed by him is only physical disability and not functional disability.

Under such circumstances,
considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 13% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 40% disability of left lower limb, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss SCCH-5 income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: It is admitted fact that, he took treatment as inpatient at Kenganar Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 30.11.2021 to 04.12.2021 i.e., for 5 days.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.14,250/- p.m.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,375/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
SCCH-5 19.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.10 medical bills for Rs.1,45,051/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 30.11.2021.
So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained left proximal tibia fracture with avlusion of fibula tip, impending compartment syndrome, which are grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against petitioner for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Further charge sheet is also filed against driver of the offending lorry by name Raj Lashkare for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

So the said SCCH-5 charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
20.

Considering the nature of the injuries, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
The Petitioner was treated as inpatient for a period of 5 days at Kenganar Hospital.
Considering the duration of treatment, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.

Per contra except denial in the written statement and oral evidence, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case,

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No.
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 3,77,910-00 2.
Pain and
sufferings 15,000-00
3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,45,051-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6. Loss of income during laid up 2,375-00 SCCH-5 period Total 5,70,336-00 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,70,336/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. Ofcourse during the course of arguments Smt.GR for respondent No.2 argued that, driver of the offending vehicle has violated the policy conditions, petitioner has not disclosed the facts, hence respondent No.1 is only liable for compensation and motor cycle hit the lorry and permission to ply the vehicle on road not produced and no permit to the offending vehicle and transit policy has not produced and owner has violated terms and conditions and PW-1 has admitted the respondent No.2 case and seal on medial bills receipts not issued SCCH-5 and as per sketch, contributory negligence has to be attracted, PW-2 is not a treated Doctor etc., but said arguments have not proved by the respondent respondent No.2 by adducing evidence.

Hence, any amount of arguments addressed by the Smt.GR counsel have not supports their case, because Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against respondent No.1 vehicle i.e., offending vehicle owner and driver and as per the policy,
respondent No.2 has issued policy dated 26.11.2021 to the offending vehicle and petitioner has proved his case as per the petition and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
